name: You are not the only doer
meaning: Every action has many causes: the body, the agent, the instruments, the efforts and the unseen; one who sees oneself as the sole doer does not see truly.
applies_when: Someone is crushed by blaming themselves entirely for an outcome, or inflated by taking all the credit.
misleads_when: It is used to dodge responsibility for one's own choices.
modern_application: List every factor that contributed to the outcome. Mark which ones were yours. Take responsibility for those, and only those.

name: The victory was not yours alone
meaning: In the Kena parable the gods claim a victory as their own; a single blade of grass humbles their powers, and they learn the victory was Brahman's.
applies_when: Success has made someone proud, dismissive of the team, or blind to luck and help.
misleads_when: It is used to deny someone fair credit for their real contribution.
modern_application: After a success, thank by name three people or circumstances without which it would not have happened.

name: Humility comes first
meaning: Humility and lack of pretence head the Gita's list of what knowledge is; the wise are free of pride and delusion.
applies_when: Pride is damaging relationships, learning or judgement.
misleads_when: It is used to make someone shrink or deny their own abilities.
modern_application: Ask someone who sees you clearly for one thing you could do better, and thank them without defending yourself.

name: Beware the intoxication of wealth
meaning: The demonic mindset says 'this is mine, that will be mine too; I am rich and well-born, who is like me?' Deluded by wealth, the careless see only this world.
applies_when: Money or status is changing how someone treats others, or blinding them to anything beyond acquisition.
misleads_when: It is used to condemn people simply for being wealthy, or to romanticise poverty.
modern_application: Notice when you think 'who is like me?'. Treat it as a warning light, and do something for someone with less power than you.

name: Do not covet another's wealth
meaning: The Isha's first verse: all this belongs to the Lord, so enjoy through letting go, and do not covet anyone's wealth.
applies_when: Envy of others' possessions, inheritance disputes, or wanting what someone else has.
misleads_when: It is used to tell people not to claim what is rightfully theirs, such as wages or a fair share of an inheritance.
modern_application: When envy rises, list three things you already have that you would not trade. Then ask what you actually need, not what they have.

name: Enjoy through letting go
meaning: Everything is to be seen as belonging to the Lord; enjoyment comes through renunciation, not possession.
applies_when: Someone's enjoyment is spoiled by fear of losing what they have.
misleads_when: It is used to pressure someone to give up what they need.
modern_application: Give away or lend one thing you have been clinging to, and notice how it feels.

name: Content with what comes unsought
meaning: Content with whatever comes unsought, beyond the pairs of opposites, free of envy, the same in success and failure: such a person is not bound even when acting.
applies_when: Someone is restless for more even when their needs are met.
misleads_when: It is used to discourage legitimate ambition or effort to improve one's situation.
modern_application: For one day, notice and appreciate each good thing that arrives without your effort.

name: Free of envy
meaning: Freedom from envy and malice marks the steady person; the rajasic mind sees everyone as separate and competing.
applies_when: Comparison with peers, siblings or colleagues is causing bitterness.
misleads_when: It is used to dismiss real unfairness behind someone's feeling of envy.
modern_application: Mute or step back from one source of constant comparison for a week, and see how you feel.

name: Beware hypocrisy and display
meaning: Hypocrisy, arrogance and conceit are marks of the demonic nature; religious acts done for show are 'in name only'.
applies_when: Someone notices a gap between what they show and what they are, in themselves or a community.
misleads_when: It is used to accuse others rather than examine oneself.
modern_application: Pick one area where your public image is ahead of your private reality. Close the gap from the private side.

name: Learning is not the same as wisdom
meaning: Those who think themselves wise and learned while living in ignorance are the blind leading the blind; the unwise delight in the letter of scripture.
applies_when: Someone, or someone they follow, uses knowledge or qualifications as a substitute for good judgement or character.
misleads_when: It is used to dismiss education or expertise.
modern_application: Ask of any advice: does this person live what they teach? Weigh their advice by that.

name: Success from action comes quickly, and ends
meaning: People pursue success through action because it comes quickly; but its fruits come to an end, and those who reach heaven return when their merit is spent.
applies_when: Someone is building their whole life around quick wins.
misleads_when: It is used to dismiss success as worthless.
modern_application: Alongside your short-term goals, keep one long-term aim that does not depend on quick results.

name: Ego that will not listen leads to ruin
meaning: With a steady mind you cross every difficulty; but if out of ego you will not listen, you will be lost.
applies_when: Someone is refusing all advice out of pride, or is about to ignore a clear warning.
misleads_when: It is used to demand obedience to any authority. Listening is not the same as obeying.
modern_application: Write down the advice you have been resisting most, and list one way it might be right.

name: Gold and stone alike
meaning: To the steady yogi, a lump of earth, a stone and gold are the same; their worth does not rule the mind.
applies_when: Money worries or money greed are dominating someone's thinking.
misleads_when: It is used to excuse financial irresponsibility towards dependants.
modern_application: Set a fixed time once a week to handle money, and keep it out of your mind the rest of the week.

name: Trust alongside effort
meaning: To those who are steadily devoted, God brings what they lack and protects what they have; even while doing all kinds of action, one who takes refuge reaches the lasting state.
applies_when: Financial or practical anxiety is overwhelming someone who is already doing what they can.
misleads_when: It is used as a reason not to plan, save, work or seek practical help.
modern_application: Do the next practical step (make the call, fill the form), then consciously set the worry down until the next step is due.

name: Steady and enthusiastic, without 'I'
meaning: The best kind of doer is free of attachment, does not keep saying 'I', is full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and is unchanged by success and failure.
applies_when: Someone wants a model of how to work hard without ego or burnout.
misleads_when: It is used to judge others harshly as 'rajasic' or 'tamasic'.
modern_application: Look at your last project. Where were you steady, where enthusiastic, and where was it mostly about 'me'?

name: Praise and blame alike
meaning: The one beyond the gunas is the same in praise and blame, honour and dishonour, towards friend and foe.
applies_when: Social media reactions, reviews or gossip are steering someone's choices.
misleads_when: It is used to ignore all feedback.
modern_application: Decide what you would do if no one would ever praise or blame you for it. Do that.
